newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka interest rates seen lower-Bank of Ceylon.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka interest rates seen lower-Bank of Ceylon.

text.p: Sri Lankan interest rates are falling and likely to decline further in future, the state-owned Bank of Ceylon said.

The annual report from the bank's economic research division, received by Reuters on Wednesday, said commercial banks' weighted average prime lending rates fell to 18.4 percent at the end of 1996, from 20.1 percent a year before.
"Interest rates are sloping downwards. The analysis of interest rate movements indicates that the rates have fallen by one to three percent since December 1996," it said.
"The Central Bank of Sri Lanka (CBSL) is intent upon bringing down the rates further," it added.
It said the lower rates were largely due to a reduction in statutory reserve requirements on rupee and foreign reserve deposits, which had helped ease rates by boosting liquidity.

"CBSL is likely to continue to adopt a monetary policy designed to achieve the objectives of reducing interest rates further, stabilizing the par value of the Sri Lanka rupee, and containing inflation," the report said.
